newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Aramco begins 1997 oil product negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco begins 1997 oil product negotiations.

text.p: State-owned Saudi Aramco has started negotiations for term supplies of refined oil products in 1997, Gulf trading sources said on Thursday.
"This is very early for Aramco...It caught everyone on the hop," one trader based in the Gulf said.
Aramco has solicited initial volume and price submissions from potential term customers for gas oil, kerosene and also fuel oil, traders said.
Naphtha term supply talks for one-year supplies beginning in January are expected later this year.
Negotiations in Saudi Arabia, Asia and Europe between Aramco and customers to finalise volumes and prices are likely to stretch out until the end of the year, traders said.
"This is the opening round in a long path of negotiations," one Gulf trader said.

The start of Aramco's annual contract talks is against a background of strong Gulf product prices which have risen close to post Gulf-War highs because of the latest U.S.-Iraq confrontation and low global heating oil inventories.
Contract price and premium levels achieved by Aramco act as an informal benchmark for other Gulf product suppliers such as Bahrain, Abu Dhabi, Kuwait and Oman.
Contract talks for product supplies out of Bahrain are not expected till December, traders said.
Aramco had approached companies to submit volume requests for gas oil and kerosene exports from Ras Tanura, Jubail, Rabigh and Yanbu by the end of this month, they added.
Aramco has not yet given any indication of how much gas oil or kerosene it will supply to the market or its pricing ideas or how regular the supplies will be.
Rising domestic middle distillate consumption has capped Aramco gas oil exports.
"There are hints that gas oil will be exported only at certain times of the year," one market source said.
Aramco had also asked some companies to submit their fuel oil volume requirements from Ras Tanura, Yanbu and Jubail, though not every company had yet received notification from Aramco.
The company firm sells seven to eight million tonnes a year of fuel oil under term contracts.

Kuwait Petroleum Corp began talks with Indian Oil Corp (IOC) officials this week to set the terms for IOC's purchases of high speed diesel and superior kerosene for the last five months and the next seven months.
